issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a method named printFarmSong() (see task description), but the provided template and the solution both declare the method as singFarmSong(). This name mismatch between the instructions and the code can confuse students about which method to implement and may cause graders/tests expecting one name to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement to refer to singFarmSong() instead of printFarmSong(), or (B) rename the method in the template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() (and update references accordingly). Ensure the UML, task text, template, and solution all use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to a method named printFarmSong() (UML and Part 3 instructions) while both the template and the reference solution provide and use a method named singFarmSong(). This naming mismatch for the same conceptual operation (playing/singing the farm song) creates a mapping confusion: students may implement or look for printFarmSong() as instructed by the text but the codebase and example usage use singFarmSong(), and automated tests or provided template scaffolding may expect the latter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either (a) change the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong() everywhere, or (b) rename the template and solution method singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() (and update all usages, tests, and Main examples) so that the textual requirements and code identifiers match.
